en.t: he shall give an inheritance to

01.r: Forbids the prince to take the people's land.
01.n: The word carries the Hebrew 'and' that opens the verse, given here as the plain 'And' before the subject.

02.n: BDB: take, take from or out of. With 'from' it means taking part of something.

03.r: The ruler of Israel in the vision of the restored land.
03.n: Gesenius: literally 'lifted up'; a prince, a general name used both of kings, and cites this part of Ezekiel for it.

04.r: Any part of the land that families hold by inheritance.
04.n: Gesenius notes this noun is often used of the territory assigned to each tribe.

05.r: The ordinary Israelites, as distinct from the prince.
05.n: BDB lists 'common people' among this noun's uses.

06.r: Taking their land by force would wrong them.
06.n: Gesenius: to act violently, to oppress. Joined to 'out of their holding', it describes pushing families off their land; the JPS has 'to thrust them wrongfully out'.

07.r: The land each family holds as its own.
07.n: Gesenius: possession, especially used of the possession of lands and fields. Our register renders this word 'holding', to keep it apart from 'inheritance'.
t: to thrust them out of their possession
nor thrust them out of their possession
to thrust them ... out of their possession
to thrust them out of their possession

08.r: The prince must use his own land to provide for his heirs.
08.n: The same word as 'their holding' just before: his holding against theirs.

s: he shall give an inheritance to
09.r: The prince passes land to his sons.
09.n: The causative form of the verb 'inherit': literally 'he shall cause his sons to inherit', as the Geneva and YLT have it.
t: He is to provide an inheritance

10.r: Marks 'his sons' as the object of the verb.
10.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'he shall give an inheritance to'.

12.r: States the purpose of the rule.
12.n: BDB: purpose, intent; with what follows, a conjunction, 'so that'.

15.r: Families driven off their land would be scattered.

16.r: The LORD claims the people as his own.

17.n: The word is 'man'; STEPBible tags this occurrence with the sense 'anyone', and the brief's lexicon lists 'each' among its senses.

01.n: οὐ μή, a strong double negative: 'shall by no means'.

03.n: ἀφηγέομαι, lead: 'the one leading', the leader.

06.n: καταδυναστεύω, oppress, lord it over. The Greek has nothing for 'out of their holding'.

08.n: κατάσχεσις, a holding, a possession held fast; it comes from κατέχω, hold fast.
